title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Sharia Islam Worship And Supplication

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is without equal in the religion he brought, in worship, in prayer, and in knowing Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the law he brought?
questions.answer: It says that no other law is like it in fairness, careful guidance, and lasting influence over many people for a very long time.

questions.question: Why is it important that he was unlettered?
questions.answer: It makes his achievement even more amazing, because he brought great guidance without learning it from books or teachers in the usual way.

questions.question: How did Islam help people, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It guided their minds, gave safety and direction, cleaned and brightened their hearts, trained their souls, and helped their spirits grow.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s worship?
questions.answer: It says he was the best example in doing acts of worship, being careful of Allah, and carrying out worship fully even during hard times.

questions.question: How is his worship shown to be special?
questions.answer: He practiced every part of worship in the best way and did not copy another person.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his prayers and du'as?
questions.answer: It says his prayers show a very deep knowledge of Allah that later saints and people of spiritual understanding could not reach together.

questions.question: What does this teach us about the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: It teaches that this du'a is very special and has no equal in the way it speaks about Allah.

questions.question: If later holy people could not match his knowledge of Allah in prayer, what can we infer about him?
questions.answer: We can infer that he had a very high and unique closeness in knowing and describing his Lord.

questions.question: Which parts of life does the passage use to show his greatness?
questions.answer: It uses religious law, Islam as a way of life, worship, piety, and supplication.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kinds of things did the Prophet bring to people?
questions.answer: He brought a sacred law, Islam, worship, a mission, a call to truth, and faith.

questions.question: How does the passage describe these things compared with anything else?
questions.answer: It says nothing equal to them exists, and nothing more complete can exist.

questions.question: What proof from history is given for the strength of his law?
questions.answer: It ruled a large part of humanity with justice and care for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What effect did Islam have on people in each century?
questions.answer: It taught their minds, protected and guided them, purified their hearts, trained their inner selves, and helped them progress.

questions.question: What can we learn from the passage about true religion?
questions.answer: True religion helps the whole person, not only actions but also the mind, heart, soul, and spirit.

questions.question: How did the Prophet act in worship while living an active and difficult life?
questions.answer: He still gave full attention to worship and carried out its deepest meanings.

questions.question: What is meant by saying he joined the beginning and end of worship perfectly?
questions.answer: It means he completed worship in the best way from start to finish, with full servanthood to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that he did not imitate anyone?
questions.answer: To show that his worship was original, complete, and unmatched.

questions.question: What special example of his prayer is named in the passage?
questions.answer: The Jawshan al-Kabir is named.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage lead the reader to about the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: It leads the reader to see that he is unmatched in guiding people and in serving Allah.

questions.question: Who is the passage mainly talking about?
questions.answer: It is mainly talking about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.question: In what area does the passage first say he has no equal?
questions.answer: It first says he has no equal in the law and religion he brought.

questions.question: How long does the passage say his law has guided people?
questions.answer: It says for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: About how many people in each century are said to have been guided by Islam?
questions.answer: About three hundred million people.

questions.question: What are two ways Islam helped people's inner lives in the passage?
questions.answer: It purified hearts and trained souls.

questions.question: What are two ways Islam helped people's growth in the passage?
questions.answer: It educated minds and helped spirits advance.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his level of taqwa?
questions.answer: It says he was first and greatest in piety and fearing Allah.

questions.question: Did the passage present his worship as careless or careful? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents his worship as very careful, full, and deep.

questions.question: How does the passage compare his knowledge of Allah in prayer with that of later saints?
questions.answer: It says later saints and people of deep spiritual knowledge could not reach his level even together.

questions.question: What overall picture of the Prophet ﷺ does this passage give?
questions.answer: It gives the picture of a messenger who is unmatched in religion, character of worship, and deep knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: What claim does the passage repeat in different ways about the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: It keeps saying that he has no rival and no equal.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the system of life he brought?
questions.answer: It says it is complete, unmatched, and impossible to surpass.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention justice and precision in his law?
questions.answer: To show that his religion gives balanced and careful guidance for human life.

questions.question: How did Islam serve as both a guide and a refuge?
questions.answer: It showed people the right way and also gave them safety and support.

questions.question: What does the passage show about worship during hardship?
questions.answer: It shows that even during struggle and busy work, worship should still be done sincerely and fully.

questions.question: What makes his worship different from ordinary worship?
questions.answer: He practiced all forms of it first and best, with deep awareness of Allah.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage gives for saying his prayer is unmatched?
questions.answer: His prayers describe Allah with a depth of understanding that others could not equal.

questions.question: What does mentioning many saints and knowers of Allah add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that even very righteous and wise people after him did not reach his level.

questions.question: What can a student infer about the place of du'a from this passage?
questions.answer: Du'a is very important because it shows a servant’s knowledge of Allah and closeness to Him.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: The passage says the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is uniquely excellent in the religion he brought and in the way he worshiped and knew Allah.

questions.question: What six things does the passage say the Prophet brought?
questions.answer: A sacred law, Islam, worship, a mission, a call, and faith.

questions.question: How does the passage support the greatness of his law with a real-world example?
questions.answer: It points to its long rule over many people in a just and careful way.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam did for people’s hearts?
questions.answer: It brightened and cleansed them.

questions.question: What does the passage say Islam did for people’s souls and spirits?
questions.answer: It trained their souls and helped their spirits move forward.

questions.question: How was the Prophet’s worship connected to his daily struggles?
questions.answer: Even while facing constant effort and difficulty, he still worshiped with full care.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where he learned his worship style from?
questions.answer: It says he did not copy it from anyone.

questions.question: Which prayer book or du'a is used as an example of his excellence in supplication?
questions.answer: The Jawshan al-Kabir.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his description of his Lord in that du'a?
questions.answer: It says he described his Lord with a level of understanding others could not match.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a treatise about supplicatory prayer?
questions.answer: To point readers to an explanation of part of the meanings found in that great du'a.

questions.question: Based on the whole passage, what is one important lesson for Muslim students?
questions.answer: We should respect the Prophet ﷺ deeply and try to follow his example in worship, du'a, and obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What is the first subject discussed in this passage about the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: The first subject is the unmatched religion and law that he brought.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that his message is presented as unique?
questions.answer: It says there is nothing like it and nothing better than it.

questions.question: How does the passage show the lasting power of his message?
questions.answer: It says it guided huge numbers of people across many centuries.

questions.question: What parts of a person were changed by Islam according to the passage?
questions.answer: The mind, heart, soul, and spirit were changed.

questions.question: In worship, what rank does the passage give to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: It gives him the highest rank and says he was the leading example.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about worship and attention?
questions.answer: Worship should be done carefully, fully, and with understanding, not carelessly.

questions.question: What does the word “gnosis” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: It means deep knowing and understanding of Allah.

questions.question: Who could not reach his level in this deep knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: The saints and spiritually wise people who came after him could not reach it, even together.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the value of the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: It suggests it is a very great and unmatched du'a.

questions.question: Why does all of this strengthen a Muslim’s love for the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: Because it shows his excellence in guiding people, worshiping Allah, and teaching the truth in the most complete way.
